page: Microsoft Azure M128 is a memory-optimized server belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 128 dedicated vCPUs, which correspond to 64 physical cores with 2 threads per core operating at 2.7 GHz. The processor includes 38 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA instructions. It is equipped with 2048.0 GB of RAM, providing 16.0 GB of memory per physical core, and bundles a massive 14680 GB local SSD storage array. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data highlights a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression rank in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core tests, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and PassMark CPU evaluations. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, with uncached large-block read operations reaching top-tier status in the top 10% at 426.47 GB/sec, and cached small-block reads and large-block writes scoring in the top 25%. Database operations and Redis SET operations demonstrate strong throughput, while LLM inference shows average prompt processing but poor text generation speeds.

Given its massive memory footprint and high-capacity local SSD storage, the M128 offers high resource density for memory-bound enterprise workloads. The qualitative cost efficiency is centered on its ability to consolidate large-scale databases and memory-intensive applications onto a single node, offsetting the lower single-core performance with massive parallel processing capacity. This server is highly suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, heavy multi-threaded software compilation, and data-intensive enterprise applications.
